chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The menstruating woman wears Ihram while she does not pray.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. When the time comes (for her purity), let her wear Ihram.'

key_terms.تُحْرِمُ: She enters the state of Ihram
key_terms.لِتُحْرِمْ: Let her wear Ihram / Let her enter Ihram

ai.seo_question: Does a menstruating woman need to end her Ihram state, or can she remain in it until she becomes pure?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that menstruation does not invalidate the state of Ihram, as the prohibition of prayer is distinct from the prohibition of entering the sacred state. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs the woman to enter Ihram at the proper time and remain in it, only resuming the ritual prayers once she achieves purity, thereby distinguishing between the physical state of Ihram and the ritual act of Salah.
